signals.name: regexSteps
signals.quantity: total number of regex NFA node evaluations (each Pattern$Node.match() call is one backtracking step in the regex engine)
locations: java.util.regex.Pattern$Node#match (base class and all inner-class overrides such as Pattern$Curly#match, Pattern$GroupHead#match, Pattern$Loop#match, etc.) — cost is incurred every time the NFA tries or retries a node during Matcher.matches() called at VFSURIValidator line 243
signals.storage: ThreadLocal<long[]> in regexmeasure.RegexStepCounter (single-element array, index 0 holds the count; class placed on bootstrap classpath via Instrumentation.appendToBootstrapClassLoaderSearch so java.base classes can call it)
signals.reset: V1Guidance.getInput() calls RegexStepCounter.reset() before returning the input stream
signals.read: V1Guidance.handleResult() calls RegexStepCounter.get() and stores the value as lastRegexSteps

plans.retention: Hill-climb: always retain the input that produced the highest regexSteps as bestInput. All mutations derive from bestInput. Plateau escape: after 1000 consecutive trials with no improvement, also accept inputs with regexSteps >= 90% of the best AND byte length strictly greater than bestInput, to encourage growth toward the input_bytes limit. The seed input is ftp://a:a@a:a@a/! which triggers a small but non-zero regexSteps to bootstrap the gradient.
mutation: ByteFlip (10%): flip one random byte to a random value in [0,255]
ByteInsert (10%): insert one random byte at a random position
ByteDelete (5%): delete one random byte (only if length > 10)
ChunkRepeat (30%): select a random contiguous chunk of 1-64 bytes, duplicate it 2-8 times in place — this is the dominant operator because the ReDoS cost grows with repeated colon/at-sign sequences

DictInsert (25%): insert a dictionary token at a random position — tokens extracted from source lines 235-236: protocol prefixes (ftp://, sftp://, http://, https://, webdav://, smb://, and uppercase variants), delimiter pairs (a:, a@), single delimiters (:, @, /), and the non-matching terminator (!)
DictReplace (10%): overwrite bytes at a random position with a dictionary token
Crossover (10%): splice a random-length segment from the seed input into a random position in the current input
